text:
Mark Stone is two points from the top of the Golden Knights' career scoring list, which says a lot about a player Ottawa took 178th overall in 2010. He has 10 goals and 20 points in 21 games, half of them on the power play, and he is still the forward Vegas trusts in every situation.

Ten goals on 7.4 expected, shooting 26%, is the number that will come down. He shot 22% last season, so he has always finished better than most, but the Golden Knights have also scored almost 11 goals more than expected with him on the ice. The last ten games (five points on 10.2 expected) look like the luck evening out.

Evolving-Hockey ranked him third among all forwards last season at 4.1 wins above replacement, and the reason was two-way: opponents got noticeably fewer chances with him out there, and he draws more penalties than he takes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 96th percentile among forwards in setting up shots. At 34 the shooting percentage will drift. The hockey sense hasn't.
